newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks seen falling on tightening liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks seen falling on tightening liquidity.

text.p: Seoul stocks are expected to fall on Friday as troubles at the Kia Group cause bottlenecks in the money markets, brokers said.
"Financial institutions have turned extremely skittish. Fund flows are tightening despite the central bank's repo operations," said Kim Choon-kwon of Daewoo Securities.
The composite stock index ended 2.03 percent or 15.33 points lower at 739.72 on Wednesday.
Yields for three-year corporates, South Korea's benchmark interest rate, rose to 12.05 percent on Wednesday from 11.95 percent on Tuesday.
